newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond ylds test higher, tired of RBA wait.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond ylds test higher, tired of RBA wait.

text.p: *Australian bonds yields tested higher during the afternoon session as the market showed some impatience waiting for next week's RBA board meeting and expected cut in official rates.
*Immediate focus on U.S. employment costs index.

Australian bond yields tested higher during the afternoon session as the market showed some impatience waiting for the August 5 Reserve Bank board meeting and expected cut in official interest rates the day after.
Traders said the market was also consolidating after today's A$500 million Treasury bond tender, which while reasonably well received, did little to revive general lacklustre conditions.

Some traders are also doubting whether confirmation of the 1/2 point cut in current official 5.5 percent rates would necessarily mean the market's recent strong rally would spark back into action with the move already priced in.

"Next Wednesday (August 6) could turn out to be a bit of a non-event if they go ahead with the cut. The labour force data the next day could have more importance as it may indicate whether there will be another easing," said one bond trader at a European bank based in Sydney.

In the meantime, and apart from Thursday's local June retail sales data, the market will be largely following events in the U.S. starting later today with the release of the second quarter employment costs index.
Forecasts centre on a 0.8 percent rise, according to a Reuters survey of economists.

"This outcome would support the view that labour costs in the U.S. are accelerating, albeit at a very modest pace. A rise of this order would not be large enough to place an August FOMC rate hike on the agenda," said David Bassanese, senior economist at Bankers Trust Australia.
Other U.S. data this week included July non-farm payrolls on Friday.

The local market underperformed against the dollar bloc, particularly versus the U.S. market, which is anticipating a favourable outcome to the ECI Index. New Zealand debt partially recovered in tandam with the N.Z. dollar, having made a severe underperformance against the bloc initially.
